audit_items.proof_trace: The RPC `record_attendance_by_card` reads the user's global all-time last attendance record with no date filter (`ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1`), then toggles it. If a user's last record is `'in'` from a prior day (e.g., forgot to punch out, auto-logout failed), the first punch of a new day is computed as `'out'` and inserted with today's date — directly violating `first_record(u,d).type == 'in'`. Additionally, no serialization guard (no `SELECT FOR UPDATE`) exists in the RPC, so two near-simultaneous NFC taps can both read the same last type and insert duplicate consecutive types, breaking the alternation invariant.
audit_items.attack_scenario: User is in `'in'` state when day changes (auto-logout not triggered — `get_currently_in_user_ids` RPC is absent from all migration files suggesting unreliable deployment); next day's first kiosk punch inserts `type='out'` as the first daily record, corrupting session-time calculations in `getOverallStats` and `getUserAttendanceStats` which assume index-0 per user is always 'in'.
